proposals.before: Emperor Gongmin Hui—Zhu Yunwen—bore the tabooed name Yunwen.
proposals.after: Emperor Gongmin Hui bore the tabooed name Yunwen.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 恭閔惠皇帝諱允炆 names only the posthumous title and the tabooed given name; Zhu Yunwen is an inserted surname-plus-given not present in the source.

proposals.before: On guimao of the twelfth month He Fu routed and slew Dao Gan Meng, and Lucian was brought to peace.
proposals.after: On guimao of the twelfth month He Fu routed and slew Dao Gan Meng, and Luchuan was brought to peace.
proposals.reason: 麓川 is the toponym Luchuan, not the personal name Lucian.

proposals.before: On the guimao day of the twelfth month, He Fu defeated and beheaded Dao Gan Meng; Lucian was pacified.
proposals.after: On the guimao day of the twelfth month, He Fu defeated and beheaded Dao Gan Meng; Luchuan was pacified.
proposals.reason: 麓川 is the toponym Luchuan, not the personal name Lucian.

proposals.before: His younger brothers Yun Teng were enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, Yun Jie as Prince of Heng, and Yun Xi as Prince of Xu.
proposals.after: His younger brother Yun Teng was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, Yun Jie as Prince of Heng, and Yun Xi as Prince of Xu.
proposals.reason: The literal rendering makes a plural verb agree with the first brother's name alone; the Chinese lists three brothers with three fiefs.

proposals.before: In the sixth month Prince Min Zhu Zhen was stripped of rank and exiled to Zhangzhou.
proposals.after: In the sixth month Prince Min Zhu Pian was stripped of rank and exiled to Zhangzhou.
proposals.reason: 楩 is Pian, not Zhen; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese character.

proposals.before: Chief steward Ge Cheng, Commander Lu Zhen, and Reader Yu Fengchen died defending the city.
proposals.after: Chief steward Ge Cheng, Commander Lu Zhen, and Reader Yu Fengchen died in the affair.
proposals.reason: 死之 means they died in the affair; the Chinese does not say they died defending a city.

proposals.before: The edict said: "The state has met misfortune; bone kin of the Zhou lineage have repeatedly plotted usurpation.
proposals.after: The edict said: "The state has met misfortune; close flesh-and-blood kin have repeatedly plotted usurpation.
proposals.reason: 周親 means close kin, not members of a Zhou lineage; the literal rendering invents a dynastic name.

proposals.before: In the fifth month, on the xinwei day, Li Jinglong rushed to Jinan.
proposals.after: In the fifth month, on the xinwei day, he rushed to Jinan.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 奔濟南 has a silent subject; the idiomatic line invents the personal name Li Jinglong.

proposals.before: On the jiashen day, Xu Huihu, Duke of Wei, took the field to relieve Shandong.
proposals.after: On the jiashen day, Xu Huizu, Duke of Wei, took the field to relieve Shandong.
proposals.reason: 輝祖 is Huizu, not Huihu; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese.

proposals.before: On the jiaxu day, Xu Huihu and his colleagues broke the Yan army at Qimei Mountain and killed their general Li Bin; the Yan troops wavered and talked of marching north again.
proposals.after: On the jiaxu day, Xu Huizu and his colleagues broke the Yan army at Qimei Mountain and killed their general Li Bin; the Yan troops wavered and talked of marching north again.
proposals.reason: 輝祖 is Huizu, not Huihu.

proposals.before: Just then the emperor heard a rumor that the Yan army had already withdrawn north; he recalled Xu Huihu, leaving He Fu's force stranded alone.
proposals.after: Just then the emperor heard a rumor that the Yan army had already withdrawn north; he recalled Xu Huizu, leaving He Fu's force stranded alone.
proposals.reason: 輝祖 is Huizu, not Huihu.

proposals.before: On the xinyou day, the princes were ordered to man separate sectors of the capital; Li Jinglong, Minister of War Ru Yao, and Commander Wang Zuo were sent to the Yan camp to plead the old terms again.
proposals.after: On the xinyou day, the princes were ordered to man separate sectors of the capital; Li Jinglong, Minister of War Ru Chang, and Commander Wang Zuo were sent to the Yan camp to plead the old terms again.
proposals.reason: 茹瑺 is Ru Chang (瑺 = Chang), not Ru Yao; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese.

proposals.before: On the xinyou day, the princes were ordered to guard the capital by separate assignments; Li Jinglong together with Minister of War Ru Yao and Commander Wang Zuo were sent to the Yan army to renew the previous agreement.
proposals.after: On the xinyou day, the princes were ordered to guard the capital by separate assignments; Li Jinglong together with Minister of War Ru Chang and Commander Wang Zuo were sent to the Yan army to renew the previous agreement.
proposals.reason: 茹瑺 is Ru Chang (瑺 = Chang), not Ru Yao; the given-name romanization does not match the Chinese.

decisions.reason: s0001 恭閔惠皇帝諱允炆 gives only the posthumous title and tabooed given name 允炆; the inserted surname-plus-given Zhu Yunwen is not in the Chinese.
s0021 麓川平 names the place Luchuan pacified after He Fu slew Dao Gan Meng; Lucian is a false personal-name reading of 麓川.
The same 麓川 in s0021 is the toponym Luchuan; the literal’s Lucian invents a personal name.

s0029 封弟允熥為吳王，允熞衡王，允熙徐王 lists three younger brothers with three fiefs; plural brothers with were attached only to Yun Teng is ungrammatical, and the proposed singular elliptical listing restores readable English without changing the facts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封弟允熥為吳王，允熞衡王，允熙徐王

decisions.reason: s0045 岷王楩 has given name 楩 (Pian); Zhen does not match the character.
s0050 ends 死之, the standard formula for dying in the affair; the Chinese does not say they died defending a city.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 長史葛誠、指揮盧振、教授余逢辰死之

decisions.reason: s0061 骨肉周親 means close flesh-and-blood kin (周親 = intimate relatives); reading 周 as the Zhou lineage invents a dynastic name absent from the phrase.
s0101 奔濟南 has a silent subject, but s0100 ends 景隆奔德州 and s0103 resumes 景隆敗績於城下; naming Li Jinglong correctly resolves the same agent and is accurate idiomatic English, not a false insertion.
s0150 徐輝祖 is Xu Huizu; Huihu misreads 輝祖.
s0157 徐輝祖 again requires Huizu, not Huihu.
s0158 召輝祖還 refers to the same 輝祖 (Huizu); Huihu is wrong.
s0173 兵部尚書茹瑺 has given name 瑺 (Chang); Yao does not match the character.
The same 茹瑺 in s0173 must be Ru Chang in the literal field as well.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Zhu Yunwen came only from the inserted surname-plus-given in the bad idiomatic; s0001 supports 允炆 / Yunwen, so the personal-name claim’s en must drop Zhu while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0005 restores Pian for 楩; the personal-name claim’s Zhu Zhen came only from the bad romanization.
Accepted r0005 shows the title English must use Pian for 楩, matching zh 岷王楩.
Accepted r0009 restores Xu Huizu for 徐輝祖; the personal-name claim’s Xu Huihu came only from the bad romanization.
Accepted r0011 shows alternate English Huihu came only from misreading 輝祖; the claim must read Huizu.
Accepted r0012 restores Ru Chang for 茹瑺; the personal-name claim’s Ru Yao came only from the bad romanization.
